body_html: The 3 KB search result versus a 16,000-tool catalogue is a compelling boundary. The third-party region near miss is also a good negative test: before action_invoke, I would check provider identity and schema, not just the similarity score. Likewise, retriable: true on the OAuth error means retry after the human connection is refreshed, not loop on the same unauthorized call. Have you tried a deliberately ambiguous search where a wrong-provider tool ranks first?

children.body_html:
hadn't, so I just tried it. "List available regions" with no provider named: the top five were Lambda, CompanyEnrich, Make, Railway and SingleStore, all between 0.68 and 0.71, and DigitalOcean's region-list wasn't in the five at all. same thing with the provider named ("List DigitalOcean regions and their availability") puts digitalocean_region-list first at 0.83, with the next hit at 0.58.

so I'd add one thing to your check: look at the gap, not just the top score. 0.83 with a 0.25 gap is a confident match. 0.71 with five tools within 0.03 of each other means the query was ambiguous, and the agent should narrow it (name the provider) instead of calling the top hit. one odd detail too, the list isn't strictly sorted by score, a Daytona tool at 0.58 came back below one at 0.54, so sort it yourself before trusting the order.

and agreed on retriable, the recovery_hint was refresh_auth, so the right move is stop and ask the human, not retry.

body_html: Measuring tool search through a gateway is the kind of number people skip. A gateway in front of the agent's tools is also a natural place to log and hold risky actions, not just route them.

children.body_html: agreed, and that's the part I didn't test. the closest I got was the OAuth step, the gateway refused the DigitalOcean call until I approved the connection myself, so the agent never held the keys. but that's a one-time gate per provider, not a per-action hold. something like "pause anything that deletes or spends and ask first" would be the more interesting thing to look for next.
